beats.say: Hello! Today we learn to spot fake payment requests sent in a known supplier's name.
This is the most dangerous sentence: our bank details changed, pay the next invoice to the new account.

body.text: Dear partner,
Due to an audit we have moved our account to UlduzBank.
Please pay the September invoice (14,860 manat) to the new account:

beats.say: Such an email can even come from the supplier's real address, because their mailbox can be hijacked.
The rule is simple: call a number you already know, never the one in the email.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs in this email.

body.text: Dear partner,
Due to an audit we have moved our account to UlduzBank.
Please pay the September invoice (14,860 manat) to the new account:
Payment is due today by 16:00, the old account is being closed.
For questions call only this number: +994 50 000 72 19

spots.label: Different domain
spots.explain: The supplier's address was ofistechizat.example. The extra "-az" and other ending make it a look-alike.

spots.label: New account number
spots.explain: Changed bank details are the whole goal of this scam. Money sent there is hard to get back.

spots.label: Time pressure
spots.explain: A deadline pushes you to pay without checking. A real partner gives you time to verify.

spots.label: Number in the email
spots.explain: If you call this number, the scammer answers. Take the number from the contract instead.

scenes.title: Accounts mailbox
scenes.intro: You handle payments. Open four emails and choose the right step for each.

body.text: Hello, the September invoice is attached.
Payment as usual to the account in our contract. Regards, Sabina Karimova

actions.label: Open attachment
actions.feedback: Known address, an expected PDF invoice and the account does not change. This is normal mail.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. There is no new account and no time pressure here.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Caution is good, but there are no signs here. You can pay an expected invoice to the contract account.

body.text: Dear partner,
Due to an audit we have moved our account to UlduzBank.
Please pay the September invoice (14,860 manat) to the new account:
Payment is due today by 16:00, the old account is being closed.
For questions call only this number: +994 50 000 72 19

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right: look-alike domain, new account and a deadline. No button? Forward it to IT security.

actions.label: Reply: we accept the new account
actions.feedback: The payment would go to the scammer. Never accept new bank details by email alone.

actions.label: Reply: is this true?
actions.feedback: The scammer will reply and say yes. Only a number you already know can verify it.

body.text: Sorry, we forgot to mention it.
Please pay this invoice to our new account: AZ00ULDZ00000000400520007731
To confirm, call me on this number: +994 55 000 31 84

steps.say: The address is real. Still be careful.

actions.label: Call the number in the contract
actions.feedback: Right. A mailbox can be hijacked, but the number in your contract reaches the real supplier.

actions.label: Call the number in the email
actions.feedback: That number belongs to the scammer, who will confirm everything. Use your own records.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: The address is real, but the mailbox was hijacked. Always check new bank details separately.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Good step. Security can also warn the supplier.

body.text: Pay Kur Tikinti's advance today to their new account, they send the details tomorrow.
I am in a meeting, do not call. Anar

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. The name is the boss's, but the domain is not idare.example, and "do not call" is a warning sign.

actions.label: Call the boss on a known number
actions.feedback: Great. Even if the boss is in a meeting, a one minute check prevents a big loss.

actions.label: Reply: we pay today
actions.feedback: The money would go to the scammer. Pressure and secrecy are reasons to stop the payment.

scenes.title: Call from the supplier
scenes.intro: Soon a call comes in the supplier's name. Read what the caller says and choose your answer.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is not dangerous. What you say next matters.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That is fine too. Later call the supplier yourself on the contract number.

steps.say: Hello, Zaur Guliyev from OfisTechizat. Did you get our new details? If you do not pay today, your order stops.
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> Zaur Guliyev from OfisTechizat. Did you get our new details? If you do not pay today, uh, your order stops.

actions.label: Fine, we pay the new account today
actions.feedback: The call is part of the trap, built to back up the email. The caller's number proves nothing.

actions.label: We will check the change our own way
actions.feedback: Right. A real supplier understands a verification check.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Good choice. Now call the contract number yourself.

steps.say: Your manager agreed, I spoke to him. Send me a photo of the payment order so I can check it.
steps.spoken: Your manager agreed, I spoke to him. <breath> Send me a photo of the payment order so I can check it.

actions.label: I send the photo
actions.feedback: A payment order holds account and signature details. Scammers use them to forge new documents.

actions.label: I will call my manager myself
actions.feedback: Great. Only the manager can confirm "the manager agreed".

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. When pressure grows, ending the call is the best answer.

actions.label: Call the number in the contract
actions.feedback: Right. The real supplier will say nothing changed, and you report the scam.

actions.label: Call back the number that called
actions.feedback: That number goes to the scammer. Verify only with a number from your own records.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The scammer will try another colleague. Tell security.

scenes.prompt: Put the steps in order when new bank details arrive.

items.label: Take the number from the contract or past records
Call and ask about the change
Have a second colleague approve it

scenes.explain: Bank details change only after a check on a known number and approval by a second colleague.

question.prompt: You already sent the money to the new account. What comes first?

options.label: Call my bank at once to stop the transfer, and tell security
options.feedback: Right. The sooner the bank knows, the better the chance to stop the money.

options.label: Wait for the supplier to answer
options.feedback: Every hour moves the money further away. Waiting loses time.

options.label: Email the same address and ask for it back
options.feedback: The scammer reads that mailbox. Only the bank can stop the money.

scenes.explain: With a wrong transfer, time decides: first the bank, then security. Keep the emails as evidence.

points: When bank details change, hold the payment
Call a number you know, not the one in the email
Already paid? Call the bank and security at once
